stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: A charged capacitor $C$ discharges through a resistor $R$ and an inductor $L$. The stored energy sloshes between $C$ and $L$ while $R$ bleeds it as heat. Sweep $R$ and $C$ across the full range. Cross the critical damping threshold $R_c = 2\sqrt{L/C}$ and watch the curve shape change: oscillatory below, monotonic above.
stages.concept: The circuit obeys $L\,\ddot{q} + R\,\dot{q} + q/C = 0$. Under-damped ($R < R_c$): $u_C(t) = E\,e^{-\lambda t}\cos(\omega_1 t + \varphi)$, with envelope decay $\lambda = R/(2L)$ and pseudo-period $T \approx T_0 = 2\pi\sqrt{LC}$ when damping is weak. Two invariants: the envelope's decay rate, set by $R$; the period, set by $\sqrt{LC}$.

stages.name: Experiment
stages.instruction: A target curve is drawn in orange. Tune $R$ and $C$ so your live cyan curve overlays it. Match both the pseudo-period $T$ (peak spacing) and the envelope decay (how fast the peaks shrink).
stages.concept: Two knobs, two invariants: $T_0 = 2\pi\sqrt{LC}$ picks the period (adjust $C$), $\lambda = R/(2L)$ picks the decay (adjust $R$). Solve $C^* = T_0^{*2}/(4\pi^2 L)$ then $R^* = 2L\,\lambda^*$.

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.instruction: Only the target curve is drawn. Read $T_0^*$ off the peak spacing and estimate $\lambda^*$ from how fast successive peaks decay, compute $C^*$ and $R^*$ on paper, set the sliders, then press RUN. Match $T_0$ and $\lambda$ within $\pm 3\%$ to advance. One submit per target.
stages.concept: $T_0^* = 2\pi\sqrt{L\,C^*}$ gives $C^* = T_0^{*2}/(4\pi^2 L)$. Peak-to-peak amplitude decay: $A_{n+1}/A_n = e^{-\lambda T_0}$, so $\lambda^* = \ln(A_n/A_{n+1})/T_0^*$, then $R^* = 2L\,\lambda^*$.

labels.peek_hint: count two peaks: T is their spacing on the t-axis; then A_n+1 / A_n = exp(-lambda T), so lambda = ln(A_n/A_n+1)/T
labels.tip1: sweep R across R_c to see under-damped -> critical -> over-damped; sweep C to change period
labels.tip2: match period T (peak spacing) with C, then match envelope decay with R
labels.tip3: read T from peak spacing -> C = T^2/(4 pi^2 L); read peak-amplitude decay -> R = 2 L ln(A_n/A_n+1)/T

1.1: Try R at both extremes: low R shows sharp oscillations; high R (above R_c) shows a slow monotonic decay.
1.2: The dashed +/- E * exp(-lambda t) envelopes bound the oscillation. R controls how fast they collapse; L, C control the period.
1.3: Critical R_c = 2 sqrt(L/C). Below it: pseudo-periodic. At it: critical (fastest non-oscillatory decay). Above it: aperiodic (over-damped).

2.1: First, ignore R and adjust C until your peak spacing matches the target's peak spacing.
2.2: Then adjust R so the envelope of your curve decays at the same rate as the target's envelope.
2.3: Both invariants matter: T = 2 pi sqrt(L C) and lambda = R / (2 L). Set C first for period, then R for damping.

3.1: Peak spacing on the target = T. Compute C = T^2 / (4 pi^2 * L) with L = 0.1 H.
3.2: Peak ratio: measure two successive peak heights A_n, A_n+1. Compute lambda = ln(A_n / A_n+1) / T. Then R = 2 * L * lambda.
3.3: Set C first (period), then R (decay). The HUD shows your current T and lambda so you can align them with your paper values.
